gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-fs-fira-sans: Fira Sans reads tall and open, its s curling wide at both ends with no stroke pressing thicker than another. Abyssinica SIL stands above it with modestly modulated strokes, and that gentle serif contrast gives the sans room to look sleek.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-fs-public-sans: Public Sans has a hefty, sturdy lowercase, with broad open counters on its c and s that keep each word easy to scan. Under Abyssinica SIL, it should feel steady.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-fs-supreme: Supreme forms a thick, heavy-looking band of text, yet its letters stay held open rather than curling shut. Abyssinica SIL does dignified headings best; Supreme does crisp text.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-manrope: Abyssinica SIL leads with short ascenders over big bowls and curves a touch heavier than its joins, giving it a refined, dignified look. Manrope then keeps a single stroke width, so paragraphs should feel light and approachable.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-montserrat: Refined and dignified, Abyssinica SIL grades its weight smoothly and modestly. Montserrat does the opposite job, giving each curve generous white space and keeping its arms and legs a constant width, so text glides along like wire.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-satoshi: Approachable from the first line, Satoshi stands on a soaring x-height with a wide e that never squeezes shut. And Abyssinica SIL does its best work in headings, where its joins slim noticeably while staying sturdy against rod-like sans letters.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-switzer: Abyssinica SIL leads with short ascenders, big bowls, and diagonals slightly lighter than its verticals, which gives headings a refined, dignified presence. And Switzer handles the text, drawing tubular, wire-like letters in one width with c tips that never creep toward touching.
gen-gf-aclonica-fs-erode: Aclonica takes the heading with a large x-height, short ascenders, and wide open space between letters, giving it a modern, professional look. Erode follows below, and a slightly larger size would suit its tall middle band.
gen-gf-aclonica-fs-karma: Karma reads as a classic serif with terminals that finish well clear of the stem and a gentle modulation that never snags the eye. Beside Aclonica, its trustworthy tone is the best part.
gen-gf-aldrich-fs-erode: Aldrich draws every stroke at one thickness, with ascenders that barely clear the x-height, so headings look approachable and contemporary. Erode brings a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight to the text, which is where a tall middle band and broad apertures do their best work.
